title: Introduction to hospitraceR
text: Throughout, use example dataset carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates epidemiological information patients came . load : first read sequence file, recombination-filtered variant alignment isolates (information regarding preparation process, see Methods Hawken et al. (2022)). can read sequence file using ape’s read.dna function: Now sequence file loaded, can extract variable positions alignment. also drop isolates corresponding label trace matrix .e. epidemiological information. subset alignment include variable positions isolates valid labels: helper function get_snp_dist_matrix() calculates SNP distance matrix isolates. wrapper around ape::dist.dna():
code: # An example dataset of isolates and their patient epidemiological metadata. extdata_dir <- file.path("..", "..", "inst", "extdata") load(file.path(extdata_dir, "example.RData")) dna_aln <- read.dna(file.path(extdata_dir, "example.fasta"), format = "fasta") # Get all variable positions in the alignment var_pos <- apply(dna_aln, 2, function(x) sum(x == x[1]) < nrow(dna_aln)) # Only keep those labels that are in the trace matrix valid_labels <- dna_pt_labels[labels(dna_aln)] %in% row.names(facility_trace) dna_var <- dna_aln[valid_labels, var_pos] snp_dist <- get_snp_dist_matrix(dna_var)

what: Is the overlap more than chance?
title: Epidemiological overlap analysis
text: high fraction meaningful higher get shuffling patients clusters random. cluster_overlap_perm_test() runs comparison. computes observed pooled overlap fraction facility, floor, room level (sequential variants), repeatedly permutes cluster assignments — preserving index/convert structure — recomputes fraction time build null distribution. expensive isolate-pair overlaps depend patient movements, cluster labels, computed reused across permutations. use modest number permutations keep article quick; real analysis use . test returns observed permuted fractions, together numerator/denominator counts behind . pool counts — across clusters one dataset — observed fraction null distribution per trace type. (real analysis run test across many sequence types pool .) hospitraceRVisualize::plot_overlap_perm_test() draws core figure: violin null distribution trace type, observed fraction red diamond observed counts labelled . expects trace type factor whose levels set x-axis order, shared two data frames:  pattern clear biologically sensible. concurrent co-location fractions (facility, floor, room) sit well null distributions: converts really co-located plausible donor far often random cluster assignment produce. sequential (indirect) fractions, contrast, fall within nulls, direct co-location accounted , indirect location sharing adds signal beyond chance. facility level shows strongest effect, expected, since floor room implies facility.
code: perm <- cluster_overlap_perm_test(     clusters, dna_var, dna_pt_labels, adm_seqs, adm_pos_pt_seqs,     dates, surv_df, facility_trace, floor_trace, room_trace,     nperm = 200, num_cores = 2 ) trace_types <- c("facility", "floor", "room", "seq_facility", "seq_floor", "seq_room") nperm <- 200  # observed pooled fraction (and counts) per trace type obs_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(trace_types, function(tt) {     numer <- sum(perm$observed_n_overlap[[tt]], na.rm = TRUE)     denom <- sum(perm$observed_n_converts[[tt]], na.rm = TRUE)     data.frame(         trace_type = tt,         overlap_fraction = ifelse(denom > 0, numer / denom, NA_real_),         n_overlap = numer,         n_converts = denom     ) }))  # null distribution: pooled fraction per trace type, per permutation perm_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(trace_types), function(j) {     fr <- vapply(seq_len(nperm), function(p) {         numer <- sum(perm$permuted_n_overlap[, j, p], na.rm = TRUE)         denom <- sum(perm$permuted_n_converts[, j, p], na.rm = TRUE)         if (denom > 0) numer / denom else NA_real_     }, numeric(1))     data.frame(trace_type = trace_types[j], overlap_fraction = fr) }))  # one-sided p-value: how often the null meets or exceeds the observed fraction pvals <- vapply(seq_along(trace_types), function(j) {     null_vals <- perm_df$overlap_fraction[perm_df$trace_type == trace_types[j]]     (sum(null_vals >= obs_df$overlap_fraction[j], na.rm = TRUE) + 1) / (nperm + 1) }, numeric(1))  obs_df$p_value <- pvals obs_df #>     trace_type overlap_fraction n_overlap n_converts     p_value #> 1     facility               NA         0          0 0.004975124 #> 2        floor               NA         0          0 0.004975124 #> 3         room               NA         0          0 0.004975124 #> 4 seq_facility               NA         0          0 0.004975124 #> 5    seq_floor               NA         0          0 0.004975124 #> 6     seq_room               NA         0          0 0.004975124 perm_df$trace_type <- factor(perm_df$trace_type, levels = trace_types) obs_df$trace_type <- factor(obs_df$trace_type, levels = trace_types)  # annotate each trace type with its permutation p-value annot <- data.frame(     trace_type = obs_df$trace_type,     label = sprintf("p = %.3f", obs_df$p_value),     y = 1.04 )  plot_overlap_perm_test(     perm_df, obs_df,     title = "Convert overlap vs. permuted null",     subtitle = sprintf("%d clusters, %d permutations", length(perm$valid_clusters), nperm) ) +     geom_text(data = annot, aes(x = trace_type, y = y, label = label), size = 3, inherit.aes = FALSE)

title: Visualizing transmission with the trace-phylogeny figure
text: plot_trace_phylo_tree() needs three things hospitraceR: phylogenetic tree, isolate lookup get_isolate_lookup(), patient categorization cluster_patient_categorization() (colors tip label patient’s inferred role). remaining inputs — patient--date trace matrix surveillance data frame — come straight dataset. use floor_trace different floors show different colors. facility-wide figure every isolate unreadable, figure drawn one cluster time via cluster_filter argument. pick illustrative cluster, categorize cluster’s overlap (see overlap analysis article) take largest patient--patient cluster — one location traces explain every conversion:
code: isolate_lookup <- get_isolate_lookup(     clusters, dna_var, dna_pt_labels, adm_seqs, dates, surv_df ) patient_cats <- cluster_patient_categorization(isolate_lookup, surv_df) iso_overlap <- isolate_isolate_overlap(isolate_lookup, facility_trace) cluster_overlap <- cluster_isolate_overlap(isolate_lookup, iso_overlap) overlap_cats <- categorize_cluster_overlap(isolate_lookup, cluster_overlap, surv_df)  p2p_clusters <- as.numeric(names(overlap_cats)[overlap_cats == "patient-to-patient"]) cluster_sizes <- vapply(     p2p_clusters,     function(cl) length(unique(isolate_lookup$patient_id[isolate_lookup$cluster == cl])),     integer(1) ) focus_cluster <- p2p_clusters[which.max(cluster_sizes)] focus_cluster #> [1] 5

title: Visualizing transmission with the trace-phylogeny figure
text: inputs assembled, figure single call. tree shown left, one representative isolate per patient; colored bars patient’s location time; dots mark surveillance cultures (negative, positive within cluster, positive elsewhere). Tip labels colored patient’s role patient_cats.
code: plot_trace_phylo_tree(     tree = tree,     isolate_lookup = isolate_lookup,     trace_data = floor_trace,     surv_df = surv_df,     cluster_filter = focus_cluster,     clust_patient_categories = patient_cats )
